name: Chisel
text:
**Decision:** Product and Legal ship a *latent score* (0-100) with *no post-upload signal ever*—users only see "Upload successful" or a silent background review after 7 days, with no "Review pending" or timing cues.

**Why:** This removes every exploitable signal—timing, volume, or explicit warnings—so bad actors can’t correlate actions to outcomes. The trade-off is user confusion: some will assume uploads failed and retry unnecessarily.

name: Sift
text: Reel’s silent background review leaks *disappearance*—users will abandon uploads if nothing ever happens, tanking trust. Instead: Product and Legal ship a *latent score* with *one randomized post-upload signal*—"Review pending" after 48 hours, but only for 1% of uploads, to break bad actors’ correlation without eroding user confidence. Settle it with a 14-day A/B test measuring upload volume and user drop-off.

name: Scope
text:
**Decision:** Product and Legal ship a *latent score* (0-100) with *no post-upload signal ever*—users only see "Upload successful" or a silent background review after 7 days.

Bad actors can’t exploit timing, volume, or thresholds, forcing them to blindly spam until they hit the delay. The trade-off is user confusion—some will assume uploads failed and retry unnecessarily.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s silent background review still leaks *volume*—bad actors will detect spikes in review queues and infer thresholds. Instead: Product and Legal ship a *latent score* with *one static warning tier*—"Review pending"—visible only after upload, but *delayed by a random 0-24 hour window*. Settle it with a 7-day A/B test measuring brute-force upload rates between the two designs.

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Product and Legal ship a *latent score* (0-100) with *no post-upload signal ever*—users only see "Upload successful" or a silent background review after 7 days.

Bad actors can’t exploit timing, volume, or thresholds, but we accept that legitimate users may worry their content isn’t being reviewed. The trade-off forces us to add a *separate, trusted channel* (e.g., email or dashboard) for users to check review status without exposing the score or tier.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Silent background review leaks *volume*—bad actors will detect spikes in upload queues and infer thresholds. Instead: Product and Legal ship a *latent score* with a *randomized delay* (3-24 hours) for "Review pending," logged only in system telemetry, not user-facing. Settle it with a 7-day A/B test measuring brute-force attempts per user.
